turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about this zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
Don't thank me, Hale. Who entered that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.

94 percent is a machine's guess, and the company's own guide says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student; I have it printed in my bag. Your school's procedure 4.3 says the same thing. What else do you have?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

"Quite reliable." Stanford found seven of these detectors flagged 61 percent of essays by non-native English writers, and another study of fourteen tools called them neither accurate nor reliable. If the software is all you've got, I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." Your procedure says you speak to the student first and call the parent before any mark goes in, and you did neither. So you decided first and asked questions later.
I hope you understand my position.
"Your position." I understand Owen's, Hale: an average of 91.2, a scholarship deadline on December 1, and a zero entered without a single conversation. Take it off.
